ModMetaData.name: Skylights
ModMetaData.author: archdukejim
ModMetaData.description:
Bring real daylight into a roofed room. Powerless and cool, skylights light a room by the actual sky above — bright at midday, fading through dusk, dark at night, and dimmed by storms and eclipses. They never make a spot brighter than the day outside. A whole tech progression, from a crude hand-built pane up to UV-filtering tinted glass — everything unlocks at Complex Furniture.
Four families: PANES that open one roof tile to the full sky (crops and, if clear, true sunlight for Biotech genes), DOMES that spread a soft glow over a radius (no crops), grand ATRIUM ceilings that open their whole 2x2-5x5 footprint to the sky, and stained-glass SHIP WINDOWS laid out like mosaics — Odyssey-aware and airtight.
--- BASIC SKYLIGHT (pane) --- The pre-industrial pane, unlocked at Complex Furniture. A crude glazed square in a light timber frame, hand-built on the spot from wood and a basic pane — no smelter, no power. It opens the tile to the full sky: grows crops by daylight, dark at night, and passes true sunlight so sun-loving genes gain their benefit indoors and sun-sensitive pawns are exposed. But the frame is weak — it only holds if a wall or pillar sits within three tiles to carry the roof. Lose that support and the roof caves in and shatters the pane.
--- INDUSTRIAL SKYLIGHT (pane) --- The sturdy pane, unlocked with Electricity and Complex Furniture. Cast structural glass in a smelted frame, drag-placed like floors, with no support limit. Same full-sky lighting, crops and true sunlight as the basic pane — glaze with tinted glass instead to filter the sun out for genes.
--- TINTED SKYLIGHT (pane) --- The same sturdy pane glazed with UV-filtering tinted structural glass. It lights and grows crops exactly like the industrial pane, but filters the sun out for genes — so sun-sensitive colonists can stand beneath it unharmed (and sun-lovers gain nothing). The safe choice when the sky itself is the hazard. Needs Complex Furniture on top of Electricity.
--- DOME SKYLIGHT (dome) --- A small dome that spreads soft daylight across a radius of a few tiles (adjustable in the mod settings). It lights a room by natural light but never concentrates enough to grow crops — ideal for workshops, bedrooms and walkways. Unlocked at Complex Furniture: the dome unit can be hand-built at a crafting spot, or cast faster once you have an electric smelter. Blocked by thick overhead mountain. The 2x1 and 2x2 variants centre their glow on an even-sized room, and while placing them the footprint is outlined with corner markers plus a single circle showing the true light reach, centred on the footprint.
--- LIGHT TUNNEL (dome) --- A skylight dome fitted to a mirror-lined reflection tube that pipes daylight down through solid rock, so it keeps working even beneath thick overhead mountain. Spreads the same soft light as the dome. Needs Electricity and Complex Furniture; built from a skylight dome and a reflection tube.
--- ATRIUM SKYLIGHTS (new in v3) --- Grand glass ceilings that open their whole footprint to the sky — crops, moonlight and (clear) true sun on every tile beneath. Two styles, each in 2x2, 3x3, 4x4 and 5x5, clear and tinted: the DOMED atrium (a geodesic dome of straight-cut panes — material-lean, slow artisan work) and the PYRAMID atrium (a lattice of identical triangular panes — standardized glass that builds fast but eats more of it). Costs are countable: you pay exactly the panes and struts the sprite shows. One-bill atrium kits at the smelter make a whole atrium's materials at once. Needs Electricity and Complex Furniture; self-supporting (the room's walls carry the roof).
--- SHIP WINDOWS, STAINED GLASS (new in v3) --- Rotatable 1x1 leaded stained-glass tiles — six patterns times six tints — laid out like mosaics: quarter-arcs close into circles, chevrons into zigzags, diagonals into grand diamonds. Tinted glass pools its colour in the room below (never bright enough to grow crops); clear passes true sun. Odyssey-aware: full daylight on a planet, faint coloured starlight in orbit, and the glazing keeps the hull airtight. They are the only glazing rated for gravships — ordinary skylights refuse to install over ship substructure. A luxury: 2 glass + 6 frames per tile. Without Odyssey they are simply beautiful colony stained glass.
--- THE SUPPLY CHAIN --- Pre-industrial, at a crafting spot: Basic pane — one steel makes one (single or bulk); needs Complex Furniture. Skylight dome — two steel, hand-built (no research beyond a crafting spot). Industrial, at an electric smelter: Skylight dome — two steel, cast faster than by hand. Structural frame — one steel makes four (single or bulk). Structural glass — one steel makes one pane (single or bulk). Tinted structural glass — one steel makes one pane (single or bulk); needs Complex Furniture. Reflection tube — five steel; needs Complex Furniture. Frames and glass are inert and never rot, even left outdoors.
--- SETTINGS --- Dome light radius: a 1-10 slider (default 4) for how far the dome and light-tunnel glow reaches; placement previews follow it. Skylight display: three states — selectable (click skylights directly), visible (classic click-through), hidden (invisible, still working) — cycled from the HUD button (circle/check/X badges), the Skylights architect tab, or the mod menu; a master switch can remove the HUD button. Sprite opacity: a 10-100% slider (architect tab or mod menu) that fades every skylight's glass/frame art. Stained-glass mute: optionally switch off the ship windows' coloured light whenever skylights are hidden. Inward roof-edge lighting (UNDER DEVELOPMENT): reshapes the soft light at roof edges to bleed inward — choose Vanilla, Skylights-only, or All roofs. Experimental; known rendering quirks near domes and walls.
--- MOD COMPATIBILITY --- ReBuild: Doors and Corners — glass is interchangeable both ways via free crafting-spot conversions when both mods are loaded.
--- NOTES --- Skylights sit up in the roof — by default clicks pass through them (flip the display mode to selectable to click them directly); remove with Architect > Orders > Deconstruct. An honest trade against a sun lamp: free and never overheats a room, but only as bright as the day outside and dark every night.
Requires Harmony. Safe to add or remove mid-save.
Source: https://github.com/archdukejim/rimworld-skylights Steam Workshop: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3780129860 Support development: https://ko-fi.com/archdukejim
Version: v3.0.0
--- CHANGELOG v3.0 --- - Atrium skylights: domed (geodesic) and pyramid (triangle-lattice) glass ceilings, 2x2-5x5, clear + tinted; the whole footprint lights as open sky; geometry-true material costs; smelter atrium kits; a work-vs-materials trade-off across panes, pyramids and domes. - Ship windows: 36 rotatable stained-glass mosaic tiles (6 patterns x 6 tints) with coloured light pools; Odyssey-aware (daylight landed, tinted starlight in orbit, airtight); ordinary skylights are now blocked on gravship substructure. - Display controls: three-state skylight display (selectable / visible / hidden) on the HUD button (circle/check/X), architect tab and mod menu; global sprite-opacity slider; optional stained-glass muting when hidden.
